title: On a Book Promised and Never Sent
summary: A reader asks whether a friend's forgotten loan should be mentioned again.
author: The Correspondent's Adviser
paragraphs: A subscriber has waited two months for a book that an old friend offered to lend. She now hesitates to ask again, fearing that the request would convert a kindness into an obligation.
There is no discourtesy in a single reminder, provided it leaves the giver free to reconsider. The book may be in use, misplaced or dearer to its owner than was understood when the offer was made.

A short note can say that the title was remembered with pleasure and that no inconvenience should be taken on its account. It need not rehearse the original promise or explain why the volume is wanted.
Should the friend answer with silence, borrow another copy if one can be found. Friendship is a poor ledger, and the finest books rarely profit from being entered in it.
